header: A column chart, shared by the cards that draw one (the CPI and inflation card, the steel card): one bar for each point, round values on the left, the value on top of each bar when there are few of them (otherwise on hover or touch), a short text under it. It knows no topic: the card hands it the bars, the starting line and how to write a value. I moved it here, unchanged, from the CPI card's own file (which still exports it).

symbols.name: VALUE_PX
doc: The width a figure on a bar needs, in pixels ("104.00" in 11-pixel bold, and a little air).

members.name: tip
doc: The text of the hover read-out: "Oct 2026: 110.05".

members.name: axis
doc: The short text under the bar ("Oct", or the year at January); empty for none.

symbols.name: scaleOf
symbols.sig: export function scaleOf(values: number[], from: "zero" | number, room = 0): { lo: number; hi: number; ticks: number[]; base: number }
symbols.returns: { lo: number; hi: number; ticks: number[]; base: number }
doc: I compute the scale of a column chart here: where the bars start, the top, and the round values on the left.

symbols.name: axisKept
symbols.sig: export function axisKept(bars: Bar[], width: number, gap = 34): number[]
doc: Picks which bars get their text under the axis: those that have one, never closer than `gap` pixels; I keep the first of two that would touch.

symbols.name: ColumnChart
symbols.sig: export function ColumnChart({ bars, from, format, valueFormat, color, negativeColor = "#e11d48", ariaLabel, showValues }: { bars: Bar[]; from: "zero" | number; format: (v: number) => string; valueFormat?: (v: number) => string; color: string; negativeColor?: string; ariaLabel: string; showValues: boolean })

params.name: { bars, from, format, valueFormat, color, negativeColor = "#e11d48", ariaLabel, showValues }
params.type: { bars: Bar[]; from: "zero" | number; format: (v: number) => string; valueFormat?: (v: number) => string; color: string; negativeColor?: string; ariaLabel: string; showValues: boolean }

doc: I draw one bar for each month, with round values on the left, the value on top of each bar when there are few of them (otherwise on hover or touch), and the month (or the year) under it. `from` is where the bars start: "zero" (the rate hangs under it when below zero), or a number (the index, from 100).
